New York is actually one of the easiest big cities for couch disposal — the Department of Sanitation collects large furniture **free, with no appointment**, across all five boroughs. The entire game is timing and prep. Get those right and the city hauls it; get them wrong and you're looking at a sanitation fine that can run up to $400.

## The DSNY Rules, Exactly

- **It goes out on your trash-only day — not recycling day.** Upholstered and wood furniture rides with regular trash. (Metal furniture is the exception: that goes out with recycling.)
- **Set-out window: after 6 PM the evening before collection, before midnight.** A couch on the sidewalk outside that window is treated as illegal dumping, even if it's in front of your own building.
- **Up to six large items per collection day**, no appointment needed — DSNY discontinued scheduled large-item pickups; furniture just goes out with trash.
- **Mattresses and box springs must be sealed in plastic bags** before set-out (a sleeper sofa's mattress counts). Drugstores and hardware stores sell mattress bags.
- **DSNY will not enter your building.** Getting the couch from a fourth-floor walk-up to the curb is entirely on you — which is the real obstacle for most New Yorkers, and the part no free program solves.

Check your building's collection day with DSNY's schedule lookup before planning anything; it varies block by block.

## When Free Curbside Isn't the Answer

The DSNY route fails in three common NYC situations: **the couch can't get downstairs** (no elevator, no help, or a sectional that needs disassembly first), **the timing doesn't work** (move-out is Saturday, trash day is Wednesday), or **the couch is still good** — putting a donatable sofa out in the rain to be collected as trash is the worst outcome for a piece [a charity would have taken](/blog/eco-friendly-living/can-couch-be-donated/).

For those cases: [couch removal in New York City](/ny/new-york-city/couch-removal/) starts at $90 with the carry-out from inside your apartment included — walk-ups and all — same-day in most ZIPs when you [book before 2PM EST](/book-online/), and [donation routing](/ny/new-york-city/donation-pickup/) first for anything in good condition. Full pricing by item is in our [cost guide](/blog/junk-removal/how-much-does-couch-removal-cost/).

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Is couch pickup free in NYC?

Yes — DSNY collects furniture free with your regular trash, no appointment, up to six large items per collection day. What it doesn't include is any help getting the couch out of your apartment, and it only happens on your scheduled trash day.

### Can I put a couch on the curb in NYC any day?

No. Outside the set-out window — after 6 PM the night before your trash day — a curbside couch is illegal dumping, with fines that can reach $400. The rules apply even directly in front of your own building.

### Do I need to wrap a couch for NYC pickup?

Couches generally don't require wrapping — mattresses do (sealed plastic bags, including sleeper-sofa mattresses). One exception worth knowing: the city's health guidance calls for bed-bug-infested furniture to be sealed in plastic before disposal.

### What's the fastest way to get rid of a couch in NYC?

Booked removal — the couch leaves from inside your apartment on your schedule rather than the city's, with [same-day pickup available](/ny/new-york-city/couch-removal/) in most of the five boroughs before the 2PM EST cutoff.
